audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer has Swain's W and E swapped: spikes[0] reads "Swain's Nevermove (W) root and Vision of Empire (E)". Nevermove is E and Vision of Empire is W. The same mistake then propagates as bare slot letters into wants.you[2] ("when his W is on cooldown"), wants.foe[0] ("Root you with W"), whys[1] ("his W root"), early ("his W root") and spikes[3] ("without W up").
audit.why: Six separate lines tell the player to track the wrong cooldown. A Zac who waits out Vision of Empire (18-22s) and then slingshots into a live Nevermove loses the engage and the trade. This is the single most damaging error in the entry.
audit.corrected: Nevermove is E (12/11.5/11/10.5/10). Vision of Empire is W (22/21/20/19/18). All six references re-pointed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says when Nevermove actually roots.
audit.why: Riot's own text: "Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits." The outgoing wave is harmless — the return pass is what roots. That inverts the instinct to back away from it: walking through it toward Swain is safe, retreating keeps you in front of the return.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is described as an unconditional drain-tank window ("he wins any extended fight at 6").
audit.why: Riot's text: "This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions." It is not a fixed-duration ultimate — breaking champion contact ends it. For Zac, whose R is a disengage as much as an engage, that is the actual counterplay and it is nowhere in the entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death's Hand is treated as flat "long-range Q poke".
audit.why: Riot's text: the bolts pierce and "Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by." The bolts fan out, so the damage is a function of how close you stand — at max range one bolt lands, point-blank several do. That is a concrete positioning rule, not general poke advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Swain 6 of 7 stages and Zac zero while Zac wins 55.06%.
audit.why: Flagged in the packet. A ranged mage does own the first levels here, but the chart never lets Zac come back at all, which contradicts both the win rate and the full layer (phases[] give Zac four stages).
audit.corrected: Swain keeps levels 1-3; 4-5 and 6 become Skill, first item and 2+ items become Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal note despite Swain healing from every Soul Fragment.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently raises his maximum health. The permanent max-HP growth also feeds Zac's Unstable Matter, which deals a percentage of the target's maximum health — so the same passive that sustains Swain sharpens Zac's main damage source.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing added to whys[3]; the %HP interaction is left to the existing full-layer anti-heal line rather than duplicated.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracks only Demonic Ascension, described as "His drain. Trade when it's down."
audit.why: Swain's ultimate is not the cooldown that decides lane — Nevermove is. It is the only spell that stops a slingshot, and at 12s at rank 1 it cycles roughly four times as often as the 120s ultimate.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns to lead with Nevermove and give both real numbers.

edits.before: At 2 his W root sets up free Q damage on Zac.
edits.after: At 2 his Q stacks bolts — the closer, the worse.
By 4-5 blobs and anti-heal answer Swain's poke.

edits.before: At 6 Demonic Ascension out-drains any Zac commit.
edits.after: At 6 his R only lasts while he drains a champion.

edits.before: First item, his sustain still beats Zac's engage.
edits.after: First item, Zac's E-R kills him before R ramps.

edits.before: By 2+ items it evens — a clean flank pick flips fights.
edits.after: By 2+ items Zac's flank pick deletes Swain outright.

edits.before: Swain's Nevermove (W) root and Vision of Empire (E) let him zone and poke you from range; if you eat the W root your whole slingshot engage is wasted and he Q-chunks you for free while you're stuck.
edits.after: Swain's Nevermove (E) roots on the return pass, not on the way out — step through the outgoing wave and hold your slingshot until it passes. Death's Hand (Q) adds damage per bolt, so fight at max range.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension (R) turns Swain into a huge drain-tank — his AoE lifesteal means committing E-R into him just heals him up, so he wins any extended fight at 6.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension (R) heals off every champion it drains, so diving alone feeds it — but it only lasts while a champion is in range, so break contact and it drops.

edits.before: By 2+ items it evens — Zac's flank E-R engage can burst Swain before his R ramps if you catch him without W up, so a clean pick still flips fights.
edits.after: By 2+ items Zac takes over: flank from fog and E-R Swain before his ultimate ramps — with Nevermove down he has nothing that stops a slingshot.

edits.before: All-in only when his W is on cooldown
edits.after: All-in only when his E is on cooldown

edits.before: Root you with W and free-poke while you're stuck
edits.after: Root you with E and free-poke while you're stuck

edits.before: Levels 1-5 belong to Swain: his W root and long-range Q poke punish every approach, and if you slingshot in without dodging the root you eat free damage, so farm at range and wait out his W.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Swain: his Q poke and E root punish every approach. Nevermove roots on the way back, so step through the outgoing wave rather than running from it, then farm until blobs stabilise you.

edits.before: With two items it swings to a skill check: if you flank from fog and catch Swain before his ultimate ramps and while his W is down, your engage still kills him, so play for the clean pick.
edits.after: With two items it swings to you: flank from fog and catch Swain before his ultimate ramps and while his Nevermove is down, and your E-R simply kills him — play for the clean pick, not a stand-up fight.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Trade when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove (E): matchup-defining — 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the return pass. Bait it, then engage. - Demonic Ascension: 120s, and it drops the moment no champion is in drain range. - Your E: never spend it on chip.

notes: The W/E swap here is the highest-value fix in my slice — six lines pointed at the wrong cooldown. wants.foe[1] "Ramp Demonic Ascension to out-drain your commit" is flagged in suspectNames but the name is correct; that is a false positive. The four win[N] edits are enum-valued and cannot satisfy the +/-10% length band.
